stages.text: The sending stone at the hall cracks with a voice: the {party} are pinned by a storm far out in the wilds, and {hero} asks whether to press on or turn back.

options.label: Read the weather and guide them

critical.text: You call every turn of the storm right. {heroName} swears {town} has a weather-witch for a mayor.

success.text: They come through the storm on your word, dry enough to fight.

failure.text: Your advice takes them into the teeth of it. They come through, but it costs them.

options.label: Find a safe road on the old maps

success.text: An old drovers' road runs in the lee of the ridge. They find it.

failure.text: The old road is long gone under the scree.

options.label: Send the hall's storm-road for that country

success.text: The hall keeps a book of storm-roads, and this one is in it. They walk round the weather and rest under a cliff.

failure.text: The storm-road is out of date, but it gets them to shelter.

success.text: They turn for home. The bounty will wait for better weather.

ignored.text: The stone stays silent. They press on through the storm and pay for it.

stories.title: A toll on the road to {site}

stages.text: {hero} speaks through the stone: "A dozen spears hold the bridge on the road to {site} and want forty gold a head. We can pay, talk, or go through them. Your call, mayor."

success.text: They let the {party} pass for a song and a promise of custom. {heroName} laughs down the stone.

partial.text: They settle for a few coins and a tale of the road.

failure.text: Talk fails, and the {party} pay in full and in a temper.

options.label: Bluff that the town's riders are behind them

success.text: The spears melt into the reeds.

failure.text: Nobody believes it, and the bridge is cleared the hard way.

options.label: Name the bridge as the town's under charter

success.text: The hall's charter names the bridge as a free crossing for registered companies, and the toll-men know better than to argue with a charter.

failure.text: The toll-men can't read, and the {party} pay.

success.text: The town pays, and the {party} cross fresh.

ignored.text: No word comes, and the {party} go through them.

stages.text: "We caught one of them watching the road," {hero} sends, "a lookout from {site}. What do we do with it?"

critical.text: It tells them everything: the watch, the doors, where the leader sleeps.

success.text: It tells them the hour the watch changes.

failure.text: It spits and says nothing, then slips its bonds in the night and runs home to warn them.

success.text: It hates its masters more than it fears them, and offers to show the {party} a way in.

failure.text: It agrees to everything, which is never a good sign. They keep it tied.

success.text: They turn it loose with a warning. It runs straight back to {site}.

stages.text: Hours later the stone wakes again. "The scout says there's a back way into {site}, a drain under the north wall. It could be a trap. Do we trust it?"

options.label: Read its face for the lie

success.text: It's telling the truth. The {party} go in by the drain, behind the guards.

failure.text: It was a trap. They fight their way out of the drain.

success.text: The scout goes ahead, and the way is clear.

failure.text: It bolts at the first turning and raises the alarm.

options.label: Go in by the front as planned

success.text: They leave the scout tied to a tree, with water, and go in the honest way.

ignored.text: With no word from the mayor, they gag it and leave it. Someone finds it before they reach {site}.

stories.title: Another company on the road to {site}

stages.text: {hero} sends: "Another company is camped a mile behind us, bound for {site} too. They mean to be first in and first at the gold."

success.text: The {party} reach {site} a day ahead, tired but first.

failure.text: They run themselves ragged and get there second anyway.

options.label: Propose they go in together and split it

success.text: The rivals agree. Two companies make short work of the outer halls.

failure.text: The rivals laugh and break camp early.

options.label: Have the hall rule on whose contract it is

success.text: The hall's register shows the {party} took the contract first. The rivals turn aside, grumbling.

failure.text: The rivals were never registered and don't care. It's a race.

options.label: Let them have the first go

success.text: The {party} wait and let the rivals take the first blows.

ignored.text: The {party} race them and both arrive spent.

stages.text: "Marsh fever," {hero} sends, voice rough. "Half of us are shaking with it. We're two days from {site}."

success.text: Willow bark, boiled water and a day's rest. The fever breaks.

failure.text: The cure is half right. They go on weak.

options.label: Have the temple pray for them

success.text: The priests pray at dawn, and the fever lifts with the mist.

failure.text: The prayers bring comfort, if not a cure.

success.text: They turn back. The bounty stays on the board.

stages.text: {hero} sends: "A pedlar at the last village swears he has a map of {site}, drawn by a delver who came out alive. He wants sixty gold."

success.text: They get the map for twenty and a pair of boots.

failure.text: He won't budge, and they won't pay.

success.text: The town pays. {heroName} pores over the map by firelight.

options.label: Check his map against the library's survey

success.text: The library has the same delver's notes, and they match. The {party} know {site} before they reach it, for nothing.

failure.text: Nothing in the library matches. They pass on it.

success.text: They leave the pedlar to his next fool.

stages.text: "The map's strange," {hero} sends. "Half of it fits what we can see from here. The other half shows a door that shouldn't be there."

options.label: Work out which half is true

success.text: The odd door is real, and it goes round the worst of the halls.

failure.text: The door is a fake, and the halls behind it are full.

success.text: They use what fits and ignore the rest.

failure.text: The half that fitted was the false half. They lose a day and some blood finding out.

stories.title: A village begs the {party} for help

stages.text: {hero} sends: "A hamlet on the road to {site} has lost three children to wolves this month. They're begging us to stay a night and hunt. It'll cost us time and blood."

success.text: The {party} set out after dark with the hamlet's dogs.

options.label: Teach the hamlet to guard itself

success.text: Ditches, stakes and fires at the field edge. The hamlet thanks {town}.

failure.text: They try, but the hamlet is too few to hold a line.

success.text: The {party} leave before dawn. Nobody in the hamlet waves.

stages.text: "These are no wolves," comes {heroName}'s voice, low. "A dire beast leads them, big as a cart horse. We've found its den."

critical.text: The pack bolts into the snares, and the beast dies at the den mouth. The hamlet sends its young people to {town} to learn a trade.

success.text: The beast dies at the den mouth. Four of the hamlet's folk follow the {party} back to {town} to start over.

failure.text: They kill it, but it fights like a demon.

options.label: Fall on it while it sleeps

success.text: It never wakes. The hamlet feasts the {party} and sends word of {town}'s heroes down the valley.

failure.text: It wakes. It's a long, bad night.

success.text: The hall's bestiary names the beast and its weakness: fire and noise. It runs into the spears.

failure.text: The bestiary is wrong about this one.

ignored.text: With no word from {town}, the {party} stay a night and hunt, and go on bloodied.

stages.text: "We've scouted ahead," {hero} sends. "The way into {site} is a door carved with a riddle in an old tongue. Nobody here can read it."

success.text: The answer is 'the river'. The door rolls aside, and the guard-glyphs behind it go dark.

failure.text: Wrong answer. The glyphs flare, and they go in singed.

success.text: It's the work of an old power's masons, who always left a servants' door. They find it.

failure.text: No book you know has the carving in it.

options.label: Watch the door through the Scrying Pool

success.text: In the pool you see who comes and goes, and the word they speak at the door.

failure.text: The pool shows only mist.

options.label: Tell them to break it down

success.text: They break it down. Everything inside hears them.

ignored.text: They break the door down. Everything inside hears them.

stages.text: The hall's own stone chimes. {hero}: "A merchant on the road heard we're registered at {town}'s hall. He'll pay us to see his wagons to the next town first."

options.label: Take his gold, keep the bounty

success.text: He pays well and the detour is short.

failure.text: He haggles them down to a pittance, and the detour costs a day.

success.text: Smuggled blades for whatever holds {site}. The {party} seize them and sends the merchant packing.

failure.text: He's carrying exactly what he says.

success.text: The {party} keep to the road.

ignored.text: They take his gold and the long way round.

stages.text: {hero} sends from the road home: "{site} is done. We found folk chained in the cellars, and a chest of coin. We can't carry both through the hills."

success.text: The {party} carry the captives home. Most of them stay in {town}.

failure.text: Not all of them make it. The ones who do walk in thin and silent, and the party comes home bloodied from guarding them.

success.text: They bring the chest. The captives walk on their own, slowly, and some of them don't make it.
They build a litter and carry both, a mile at a time. {town} cheers them in.

failure.text: They try, and the hills punish them for it. The captives make it; most of the coin doesn't.

options.label: Send the hall's wagon to meet them

success.text: The hall's wagon meets them at the ford. Captives and coin both come home.

failure.text: The wagon misses them on the road. They bring the captives, and leave the gold for whoever comes next.

ignored.text: They bring the captives, and leave the coin.

stages.text: "{site} had a sword in it," {hero} sends, "black iron, warm to the touch. It talks when the fire's low. It wants to come to {town}."

success.text: A blade forged for an old power's champion, still loyal to the power.

failure.text: Its voice gets into your head through the stone. You find yourself agreeing with it.

success.text: They bury it under a cairn and don't look back. {heroName} dreams of it for a month.

stages.text: "So what do we do with it?" {heroName} asks. Behind the voice, something else whispers.

success.text: Holy water and a hot forge on the road. It screams as it breaks.

failure.text: It won't break. They bury it deep and mark the place.

options.label: Seal it in the hall's vault

success.text: Sealed and chained in the hall's vault. Collectors in three cities write to ask the price.

failure.text: The vault's wards strain against it, and something whispers in the hall at night. The hall still pays for it, in fear.

success.text: {heroName} masters it. The blade goes quiet and cuts true.

failure.text: {heroName} carries it home, and listens to it more each night.

ignored.text: They leave it where they found it, and somebody else picks it up.

stages.text: "Mayor, we're lost," {hero} sends. "Fog for two days. The guide ran off. We've food for three more."

success.text: The fog thins at night. You talk them north by the Wheel.

failure.text: Your stars are someone else's. They walk in a circle and lose a day.

success.text: A stream leads them out of the fog by evening.

failure.text: The stream sinks into a bog.

options.label: Send the Scrying Pool's sight to find them

success.text: In the pool you see them, and the road a mile to their east. They're out by noon.

failure.text: The pool shows fog.

stages.text: The stone wakes again. "We're out of the fog, on a ridge above {site}. We're tired and short of food. Go in now, rest a day, or come home?"

success.text: A deer and a cold spring. They go in fed and rested.

failure.text: Thin forage, but sleep helps.

options.label: Rouse them for one last push

success.text: You give them a speech they'll repeat to their grandchildren. They go in burning.

failure.text: The speech falls flat in the cold.

success.text: They turn for home, alive.

ignored.text: No answer comes. They find their own way out, hungry.

stages.text: "We're a day from {site}," {hero} sends. "Our caster can spend the last of the stone on a ward, or keep the spell for the fight. And the lads want a word from the mayor."

options.label: Give them a word to fight by

success.text: They'll carry your words in with them.

failure.text: {heroName} thanks you politely.

options.label: Tell the caster to cast the ward

success.text: The ward holds through the first fight.

failure.text: The ward fizzles and the spell is gone.

success.text: They keep it for the fight.
